record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: In the limit of small viscosity and heat conductivity for compressible flow, are solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations asymptotically equivalent to the corresponding Euler solutions? This includes the zero-dissipation limit near entropy-satisfying shock discontinuities, the more delicate case of contact discontinuity surfaces because of vortex-sheet instability, and the rigorous validity of Prandtl-type boundary layer theory for physically relevant flows with solid boundaries.

evidence.quote: Asymptotic equivalence between Navier-Stokes system and Euler equations for compressible fluid in the limit of small dissipation.

In the case that the underlying Euler flows are piecewise smooth with finitely many entropy satisfying shock discontinuities, it is exported that solutions to the Navier-Stokes equation will converge uniformly to the corresponding solutions to the Euler equations except around thin layers near shock discontinuities in the zero dissipation limit

The case that the solutions to the Euler equation are piecewise smooth containing contact discontinuous surfaces is more subtle due to the instability of vortex sheets ... the well-known boundary layer phenomena occur due to discrepancy of the non-slip boundary conditions for the Navier-Stokes system and the prescribed normal component of the velocity field at the boundaries for the Euler equations ... the well-known Prandtl's laminar boundary layer theory whose validity and rigorous justification are completely open

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations for a heat-conducting fluid in $d$ space dimensions,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u) &= 0,\\
\partial_t(\rho u) + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho u\otimes u) + \nabla p &= \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\bigl(\mu(\nabla u + \nabla u^\top) + \lambda(\nabla\!\cdot u)\,\mathbb{I}\bigr),\\
\partial_t(\rho E) + \nabla\!\cdot\bigl((\rho E + p)u\bigr) &= \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\bigl(\kappa\nabla\theta\bigr) + \varepsilon\,\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl((\mu(\nabla u+\nabla u^\top)+\lambda(\nabla\!\cdot u)\mathbb{I})\,u\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u$ the velocity, $\theta$ the absolute temperature, $p=p(\rho,\theta)$ the pressure, $E=\tfrac{1}{2}|u|^2+e(\rho,\theta)$ the total energy, $\mu,\lambda,\kappa>0$ are normalized transport coefficients, and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter scaling viscosity and heat conduction. Let $u^\varepsilon=(\rho^\varepsilon,u^\varepsilon,\theta^\varepsilon)$ denote a sequence of solutions, and let $\bar u=(\bar\rho,\bar u,\bar\theta)$ be a corresponding solution of the compressible Euler system obtained by setting $\varepsilon=0$.

Establish the following three statements concerning the zero-dissipation limit $\varepsilon\to 0^+$.

(a) Suppose $\bar u$ is piecewise smooth on a finite time interval $[0,T]$ with finitely many entropy-satisfying shock discontinuity surfaces. Show that, for suitably prepared initial data, $u^\varepsilon\to\bar u$ uniformly on every compact subset of the complement of an arbitrarily thin tubular neighborhood of the shock surfaces, and quantify the convergence rate.

(b) Suppose $\bar u$ is piecewise smooth and contains contact discontinuity surfaces (which are linearly degenerate and subject to vortex-sheet instability). Determine whether, and in what sense, $u^\varepsilon$ converges to $\bar u$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, in particular in space dimension $d\ge 2$ where shear may trigger Kelvin–Helmholtz-type instabilities.

(c) In a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with solid boundary $\partial\Omega$, where $u^\varepsilon$ satisfies the no-slip condition $u^\varepsilon|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ while $\bar u$ satisfies only the no-penetration condition $\bar u\cdot \nu|_{\partial\Omega}=0$, rigorously justify Prandtl's laminar boundary layer ansatz: prove that $u^\varepsilon=\bar u+U^P(t,x_\parallel,x_\perp/\sqrt{\varepsilon})+o(1)$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$, where $U^P$ solves the Prandtl boundary layer equations, for physically relevant flows.
artifact.category_tag: vanishing viscosity limit for compressible Navier-Stokes
artifact.status_search_result: The 1D zero-dissipation limit for compressible Navier–Stokes toward Euler solutions containing single shocks, rarefaction waves, contact discontinuities, and certain superpositions thereof has been largely established with explicit convergence rates. In multiple dimensions, uniqueness/stability of a planar contact discontinuity within the class of vanishing-dissipation limits from the Navier–Stokes–Fourier system has been proved (e.g., Kang–Vasseur–Wang, 2020/21), but the general multi-D case with shear (vortex-sheet instability) remains open. The rigorous justification of Prandtl's boundary layer expansion for compressible flows with no-slip boundaries in physically relevant regimes is still largely open.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of a planar contact discontinuity for 3D compressible Euler system in a class of zero dissipation limits from Navier-Stokes-Fourier system
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of a planar contact discontinuity without shear is proved for the 3D full Euler system in the class of vanishing dissipation limits of the Navier–Stokes–Fourier system.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-D contact discontinuity case partially resolved (planar, no shear).

status_evidence.title: Zero dissipation limit of the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations to piecewise smooth solutions with interacting shocks
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence to piecewise smooth Euler solutions with interacting shocks established in the zero dissipation limit.
status_evidence.claim: Shock case (1D) substantially resolved including interactions.

status_evidence.title: On the inviscid limit of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations near Onsager's regularity in bounded domains
status_evidence.snippet: Inviscid limit results in bounded domains under regularity assumptions; full Prandtl justification for compressible flows remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary-layer/Prandtl justification for compressible flows is only partially understood.
